definitions.explanation: Chicken meat that has been finely chopped or passed through a grinder. A common ingredient in Japanese cooking, especially for meatballs, dumplings, and simmered dishes.

examples.japanese: {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}でつくねを{作|つく}る。
examples.english: To make tsukune (chicken meatballs) with ground chicken.

examples.japanese: {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}は{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}よりあっさりしている。
examples.english: Ground chicken is lighter in flavor than ground pork.

examples.japanese: {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}に{生姜|しょうが}と{醤油|しょうゆ}を{混|ま}ぜて、{餃子|ぎょうざ}の{具|ぐ}にした。
examples.english: I mixed ground chicken with ginger and soy sauce to use as dumpling filling.

notes:
A compound of {鶏|とり} (chicken), ひき (ground/minced, from {挽|ひ}く 'to grind'), and {肉|にく} (meat). Also written as {鶏挽肉|とりひきにく} or {鶏挽|とりひ}き{肉|にく}, though the mixed kana-kanji spelling is most common on packaging.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}のそぼろ: crumbled seasoned chicken (for rice bowls)
- {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}のつくね: chicken meatballs
- {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}のハンバーグ: chicken hamburger patty
- {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}{百|ひゃく}グラム: 100 grams of ground chicken

RELATED WORDS:
- {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}: ground pork — fattier, used in {餃子|ぎょうざ} and {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}: ground beef — used for hamburgers and meat sauce
- {合|あい}いびき{肉|にく}: ground meat blend (usually pork and beef)
- ひき{肉|にく}: ground meat — the general term

USAGE:
{鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく} is considered the healthiest of the common ground meats due to its low fat content. It is a staple ingredient for {鶏|とり}そぼろ{丼|どん} (chicken soboro rice bowl), a popular lunch item.
